samples.summary: OAuth callback creates/updates the user record *before* the new state check, so a refused callback still mutates the database
samples.evidence: `githubAuthCallback` calls `await this.userService.findOrCreateUser({...})` at lines 115-120, and only then (line 144 / 157) decides whether the `state` is acceptable and redirects to `loginErrorUrl('oauth_state')`. The block comment at lines 132-139 claims the refusal path and the retry path are "independent: no session is issued on either path" — but a user row *is* created on both. Any unsolicited/forged callback that passport can validate against GitHub therefore provisions an account (and any profile-field updates `findOrCreateUser` performs) despite being rejected. Moving the state check above the `findOrCreateUser` call would make the refusal genuinely side-effect free.

samples.summary: `loginErrorUrl` silently produces a same-origin relative redirect when FRONTEND_URL is unset
samples.evidence: `const frontend = (this.configService.get<string>('FRONTEND_URL') ?? '').replace(/\/+$/, '');` yields `''`, so the refusal redirects to `/login?error=oauth_state` on the *backend* origin, which has no such route → 404. The success path one screen up (line 192) uses `this.configService.get('FRONTEND_URL')!` and would fail loudly instead. The `?? ''` fallback converts a misconfiguration into a silent dead-end on exactly the path the change added to avoid a dead-end.

samples.summary: `cells batch --dry-run` now bypasses `parseOutputFormat` and is no longer inside any try/catch
samples.evidence: The dry-run block was hoisted out of the `try` (lines 147-155) and `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` was placed *after* it (line 158). Consequences: (a) `cells batch --dry-run --format bogus` now exits 0 and prints the preview, while the identical command without `--dry-run` exits 1 with INVALID_FORMAT — the opposite of the ordering rule the rest of this diff establishes (`api-keys.ts:21`, `tabs.ts:53`, `files.ts:129`); (b) anything thrown by `getConfig(opts)`/`printDryRun` on that path now escapes the action instead of being enveloped by `outputError`, which is the exact failure mode the comment above it says it is fixing.

samples.summary: `--format csv` now silently rewrites data values with a leading `'` and offers no opt-out
samples.evidence: `format(data,'csv')` hard-codes `{ neutralizeFormulas: true }`. `FORMULA_TRIGGER = /^[=+\-@]/` (csv.ts:5) fires on any value starting with `+`, `-`, `=` or `@` that is not a bare number by `PLAIN_NUMBER` — e.g. a phone number `+1 (555) 123-4567`, an email-ish `@handle`, or a range label `-- total --` all become `'+1 (555)...`. Only `sheets export` got a `--raw` escape hatch; `cells get --format csv`, `docs list --format csv`, `tabs list --format csv` etc. now have no way to emit the value verbatim, so any script that pipes those CSVs reads corrupted fields. This is a behavioural regression on a pre-existing flag with no documented opt-out.

samples.summary: `neutralizeFormula` does not escape a value that already begins with `'`, so the guard is not losslessly reversible
samples.evidence: `return `'${s}`;` only ever prefixes; a cell whose text is literally `'=SUM(A1)` is emitted as `''=SUM(A1)` while a cell whose text is `=SUM(A1)` is emitted as `'=SUM(A1)`. A consumer stripping one leading quote cannot distinguish the two, and `sheets import` (which maps cells verbatim, per skills/sheets-import-export.md) will re-import the quoted form as literal text. The `--raw` flag documents the round-trip escape but the non-raw form is presented as merely 'prefixed', which is only true one way.

samples.summary: Every unconfirmed hit on the confirm page mints a fresh cookie, invalidating the Continue link of any page already open
samples.evidence: The re-prompt branch unconditionally does `res.cookie(CLI_CONFIRM_COOKIE, secret, ...)` with a new random secret. `login.ts:40-42` both auto-opens the OAuth URL *and* prints it for the user to visit — a second load (auto-open plus manual click, a reload, or a browser prefetch of the same URL) overwrites the cookie, so clicking Continue on the first page fails the `timingSafeEqualStr` check and silently re-prompts with no explanation. The CLI meanwhile just keeps waiting until the 3-minute timeout.

samples.summary: `ctx list` changes its exit code from 0 to 1 when logged out
samples.evidence: Previously the action printed `Not logged in. Run \`wafflebase login\`.` and returned (exit 0). It now throws `NotLoggedInError` into `outputError`, which sets `process.exitCode = 1`. `status` deliberately kept exit 0 for the same condition (status.ts:65-67), so the two auth-state commands now disagree, and any existing script that ran `ctx list` under `set -e` to enumerate workspaces will now abort on the logged-out case instead of reading an empty/informational result.

samples.summary: The 3-minute callback timeout is claimed to stay under the backend's 5-minute state TTL, but the two clocks start at different moments
samples.evidence: `CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS = 180_000` starts when the loopback server begins listening (before the browser is even opened). The backend's CliAuthStore entry is created only after the user clicks Continue on the new confirmation page (`github-auth.guard.ts:58`, TTL 5 min from that instant). With the confirmation hop plus a cold GitHub sign-in (2FA/device verification) the CLI can time out while the backend state is still perfectly valid, so the user's completed browser login is discarded and `wafflebase login` reports a timeout. The comment's reasoning about the TTL relationship does not hold given the new ordering.

samples.summary: `formatRecord` does not neutralize newlines in values, so a multi-line field breaks the key/value alignment
samples.evidence: `keys.map((k) => `${k.padEnd(width)}  ${cell(record[k])}`).join('\n')` — a value containing `\n` (e.g. an error `message` or a note title with an embedded newline) emits a continuation line with no key column, which a reader/parser of `--format table` will read as a malformed row. The array branch has the same issue via `cell(row[k]).padEnd(...)`.

finding.summary: `startCallbackServer` arms a 180s timer that is never cleared on its own rejection paths — the CLI hangs 3 minutes then dies on an unhandled rejection
finding.evidence: `const timeout = setTimeout(...)` (line 351) is armed before `tryListen()`. It is only cleared by the returned `close()`, which the caller can never obtain if the outer promise rejects: `reject(new Error('Failed to start callback server'))` (line 366) and `reject(err)` in the `srv.on('error')` handler (line 385, e.g. EADDRINUSE after 3 attempts, EACCES, etc.). In those paths `login`'s `await startCallbackServer(nonce)` throws before the `try { code = await waitForCallback() } finally { close() }` block is ever entered, so the timer stays armed and keeps the event loop alive. When it fires it calls `callbackReject(...)` on `callbackPromise`, which has no `.catch`/`await` attached in this path — an unhandled promise rejection, which Node ≥15 turns into a process crash. Net effect: `wafflebase login` prints its error, then sits for 180 s and exits with an unhandled-rejection stack. The previous timeout was 30_000 (diff line `-    }, 30_000;`), so this change makes an existing latent leak six times worse.

verdict.reason: The finding describes a timer armed before tryListen() at line 351 that leaks across rejection paths. That code is not present. Line 351-359 is a comment documenting exactly this hazard and why it was avoided; line 360 only declares `let timeout: ... | undefined` with no timer armed. The only setTimeout in packages/cli (grep-confirmed, single hit at login.ts:373) is inside the srv.listen callback and after the invalid-address early return at 368-372, so `reject(new Error('Failed to start callback server'))` (line 370) returns with timeout still undefined. The `srv.on('error')` reject at line 396 fires only when listen failed (EACCES, or EADDRINUSE after 3 attempts), in which case the listen callback never ran and no timer was armed; if the error arrives after a successful listen the promise is already resolved, reject is a no-op, and the caller holds close() (line 383-386, clearTimeout at 384) invoked from login's `finally { close(); }` at lines 59-61. The claimed unhandled-rejection chain therefore has no reachable path. A regression test asserting this contract exists (login-listen-failure.test.ts:49-64: mocked server emitting EACCES, 200ms wait past a 50ms timeout, expects no unhandledRejection). The CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS 30_000 -> 180_000 change at line 188 is real but cannot amplify a leak that does not exist.
